title: Who Woke First
text:
The Rooster, the Cuckoo, and the Year-Rooster had once bought a cow together. But since there was no way to divide it, and they could not agree on buying one another out, they settled on this: whoever woke first in the morning should have the cow.

So the Rooster woke first.

“Now the cow is mine!
Now the cow is mine!” said the Rooster.

When the Rooster crowed, the Cuckoo woke.
imagePrompt: At the first pale light of dawn outside a small farmhouse, the Rooster—The first to wake, quick to claim the whole cow as his prize—stands tall on a fence rail with chest puffed out, beak open mid-crow in triumph. Below him in the dew-damp yard, The Cow—the disputed purchase—stands calmly beside a rough wooden stall, chewing cud and looking unbothered, while the sleepy Cuckoo—Woken by the crow, he insists on an equal share with his repeated call—stirs in surprise from a nearby perch, feathers ruffled as he wakes to the Rooster’s shout.

title: A Call for Fairness
text:
“Half a cow!
Half a cow!” said the Cuckoo.

When he called, the Year-Rooster woke.

“My dear brothers, share as is right and fair—
Right and fair! Tsio! tsi!” said the Year-Rooster.

Now can you tell me who ought to have the cow?
imagePrompt: In the morning yard, the Cuckoo—Woken by the crow, he insists on an equal share with his repeated call—leans forward with beak open, loudly demanding his share as he faces the Rooster near The Cow. Between them, the Year-Rooster—The last to wake, he urges his brothers to share what is right and fair—has just awakened and steps in with one wing lifted in a calming, urging gesture, as The Cow stands quietly central, tethered and placid, the focus of their quarrel.
